oneLiner: 单位面积上受到的压力，反映压力作用效果。
oneLinerEn: Force per unit area; measures how concentrated a push is.
detail: 压强描述压力的集中程度，定义是 p=F/S，即垂直作用在单位面积上的力，单位帕斯卡（Pa），1 帕等于 1 牛每平方米。式中 p 为压强，F 为垂直作用在表面上的力，S 为受力面积。1 帕这个单位极小：把一枚约 50 克的鸡蛋举高 1 米大约做 0.5 焦的功，而 1 帕压在 1 平方米上的力才 1 牛，所以日常与工程里更常用千帕与兆帕，气象上还有百帕，一个标准大气压约 1013 百帕。必须把压力与压强分开：压力是力，压强讲的是作用效果，同一个力摊在越大的面积上效果越弱——菜刀磨薄、图钉做尖、注射器针头极细，都是靠减小受力面积来增大压强；铁轨下铺枕木、书包用宽背带、坦克与收割机改用履带或双胎，都是靠增大受力面积来减小压强。算几笔账就明白量级差多大：体重约 500 牛的中学生双脚站立，与地面接触面积约 350 平方厘米，对地面压强约 1.4×10⁴ 帕；踮起一只脚就翻倍到约 2.9×10⁴ 帕；芭蕾舞演员单脚脚尖着地，触地面积只有约 2 平方厘米，450 牛的体重能造出约 2.25×10⁶ 帕，比几十吨重的坦克对地压强（约 8×10⁴ 帕）大近三十倍。切菜时 10 牛的力落在 0.05 毫米宽、5 厘米长的刃口上，压强约 4×10⁶ 帕，这就是“磨刀不误砍柴工”的物理账。压强本身看不见，教材里用海绵或沙面的凹陷程度来显示它，这正是「微小量放大与转换法」条讲的转换思想。两条常见易错：一是压力不一定等于重力，斜面上物体的压力只是重力的一个分力，被手按在墙上的物体，其对墙的压力与重力毫无关系；二是 S 取实际接触面积而不是物体的表面积，公式里的 F 也必须是垂直于表面的那一个分力。液体与气体的压强另有规矩，见「液体压强」与「大气压强」两条。
detailEn: Pressure measures how concentrated a push is: p=F/S, the force acting perpendicular per unit area, in pascals, where 1 Pa is 1 N per square metre. In the formula, p is pressure, F the force normal to the surface and S the area over which it acts. One pascal is tiny — lifting a 50 g egg by a metre does about 0.5 J, yet 1 Pa pressing over a whole square metre amounts to only 1 N — so kilopascals and megapascals are the everyday units, and weather reports use hectopascals, a standard atmosphere being about 1013 hPa. Keep force and pressure apart: the force is the push, the pressure is the effect, and the same push spread wider does less. Sharpening a knife, pointing a thumbtack and using a hypodermic needle all increase pressure by shrinking the area; sleepers under rails, wide backpack straps and the tracks of tanks and harvesters reduce it by enlarging the area. Do the sums and the spread becomes memorable: a student weighing about 500 N standing on both feet (some 350 cm² of contact) exerts about 1.4×10⁴ Pa, doubling to roughly 2.9×10⁴ Pa on one foot; a ballet dancer on a single toe tip of about 2 cm² reaches some 2.25×10⁶ Pa, nearly thirty times the ground pressure of a tens-of-tonnes tank (about 8×10⁴ Pa). Slicing with 10 N along an edge 0.05 mm thick and 5 cm long gives about 4×10⁶ Pa, which is the whole point of a sharp blade. Pressure itself is invisible, so school experiments reveal it by how deep a sponge or sand dents — the conversion idea set out in the entry on amplifying and converting tiny quantities. Two common slips: the normal force need not equal weight (on a slope it is only a component, and a body pressed against a wall transfers a force with nothing to do with its weight), and S is the real contact area rather than the body's surface area, with F the component normal to that surface. Fluids follow their own rules, covered in the entries on liquid pressure and on atmospheric pressure.

oneLiner: 液体内部向各方都有压强，随深度与密度增大。
oneLinerEn: Liquids press in all directions; it grows with depth and density.
detail: 液体内部向各个方向都有压强，静止液体里某一点的压强由 p=ρgh 给出：式中 ρ 为液体密度，g 为重力加速度，h 为该点到自由液面的竖直深度。这个公式只留下两个变量——密度与深度，与液体的总重、容器的形状和底面积都无关，一池水和一根细管只要深度相同，同一深度处的压强就相同，这正是所谓“帕斯卡裂桶”的依据：相传 1646 年帕斯卡把一根细长管接到装满水的木桶上，只倒进几杯水，十米高的水柱就在桶内造出约 9.8×10⁴ 帕的压强，桶顶约 0.1 平方米的面积上受力近一吨，桶壁随之崩裂，而倾倒入的水重不过几十牛。同一深度处液体向各个方向的压强相等，因此侧壁也要受力，坝体因此做成下宽上窄，水库蓄水位越高坝底压强越大：蓄水位 175 米时坝底水压约 1.7×10⁶ 帕，合十几个大气压，潜水时每下潜约 10 米就多承受一个大气压，这正是深潜器必须用厚壳与球形舱的原因。另一条独立原理是帕斯卡定律：加在密闭液体上的压强能够大小不变地被液体向各个方向传递，于是液压机有了把手——小活塞面积若是大的百分之一，50 牛的力就能顶起 5000 牛，汽车千斤顶、挖掘机大臂、刹车踏板到制动钳的油路、机床与剪板机全走这条路；代价是小活塞要压下 100 倍的行程，力赚了距离就得赔，与「功与功率」条的账一致。第三条承载结构是连通器：上端开口、下部连通的几个容器里同种液体静止时液面等高，茶壶的嘴与壶身因此要一样高，下水道存水弯靠一段留在弯里的水封住臭气，锅炉与水箱外侧装一根玻璃水位计直接读出炉内液位，船闸则是最大号的连通器——上下游水位差数十米，先让闸室与一侧齐平再开门，三峡船闸把约 113 米的落差分成五级闸室逐级抬降，一条船过闸要三四个小时。两条易错：一是深度 h 从自由液面往下量，不是从容器底往上量，容器底与顶谁压强大的判据只有深度；二是液体压强公式不适用于气体在同一容器里的小高度差（空气密度小，几米高度的 ρgh 只有几十帕，通常忽略）。
detailEn: A liquid presses in every direction, and at rest the pressure at a point is p=ρgh, where rho is the liquid's density, g the gravitational field and h the vertical depth below the free surface. Only two variables survive — density and depth — so total weight, vessel shape and base area drop out: a pond and a slender tube give the same pressure at the same depth. That is the point of Pascal's barrel, said to have been burst around 1646 by a tall thin column of a few cups of water: ten metres of water makes about 9.8×10⁴ Pa, and over the roughly 0.1 m² lid that pushes with close to a tonne of force although the water poured in weighed only tens of newtons. Pressure at a given depth acts equally in all directions, so walls are loaded too; dams are therefore wide at the foot, and with a 175 m reservoir the bottom sees about 1.7×10⁶ Pa, some ten atmospheres — which is why divers gain one atmosphere of pressure every ten metres and deep submersibles need thick spherical hulls. A second, independent principle is Pascal's law: pressure applied to a confined liquid is transmitted unchanged in every direction, which is what gives hydraulics its lever — if the small piston has one hundredth the area, 50 N lifts 5000 N, the basis of car jacks, excavator arms, brake pedals acting on callipers, presses and shears. The price is travel: the small piston must move a hundred times farther, gain in force being paid for in distance, exactly the bookkeeping of the entry on work and power. Third comes the communicating vessels rule: like liquids standing in open, interconnected containers level out to the same height, which is why a teapot's spout matches its body, why the bend under a sink keeps a water plug against smells, why boilers carry a glass gauge reading the level directly, and why ship locks are communicating vessels at giant scale — a lock chamber is levelled with one side before the gates open, and the Three Gorges five-stage lock steps a ship through roughly 113 m of difference in three or four hours. Two slips to avoid: h is measured down from the free surface, not up from the bottom; and the formula should not be stretched to gases over a few metres, since rho for air gives only tens of pascals and the term is normally ignored.

oneLiner: 空气受重力与流动性产生压强，标准大气压约 1.01×10⁵ Pa。
oneLinerEn: Air's weight creates pressure; standard atmosphere ≈ 1.01×10⁵ Pa.
detail: 空气有质量又能够流动，被重力约束在地球周围，于是像液体一样在内部向各方产生压强，这就是大气压强，标准值约 1.01×10⁵ 帕，即 101.3 千帕。第一个把它测出来的是托里拆利：1644 年他把一根约一米长、一端封口的玻璃管灌满水银倒插进水银槽，管内液面降下一段后停住，管内外液面差约 760 毫米，上方空出的那段近乎真空，此后被称为托里拆利真空；按 p=ρgh 算，13600×9.8×0.760 恰得 1.01×10⁵ 帕。这个实验的说服力在于对照：如果水银柱是被大气压“托”住的，那么换成水就得用十米多长的管子（101325/(1000×9.8)≈10.3 米），而这直接决定了抽水机的吸程上限。1654 年格里克在马德堡当众演出，把两个铜半球合在一起抽成真空，两边各用八匹马、共十六匹才把它们拉开——半径 0.25 米的半球投影面积约 0.2 平方米，大气压在打开它之前交出约 2×10⁴ 牛、合两吨的力。吸盘、吸管与抽水机都靠气压差工作，但说法要纠正一处：用吸管喝饮料并不是把饮料“吸”上来，而是嘴里气压降低，外界大气压把液面压上去；活塞式抽水机同样靠活塞下形成低压让水被压进泵腔，而一个标准大气压最多只能把水托起约 10.3 米，这就是吸程的天花板，井太深时须把离心式水泵的叶轮下到水下、改用潜水电泵，或分级提水；高层住宅则反过来，靠屋顶水塔或二次加压供水，30 米压头约给出 2.9×10⁵ 帕，与家庭常见的 0.2 到 0.4 兆帕水压同量级。大气压随海拔升高而降低，因为头顶上那柱空气变短了：粗略地，在近地面每升高约 12 米水银柱降 1 毫米；拉萨海拔约 3650 米，气压只有约 60 千帕，水到 86 ℃ 就沸腾，饭煮不熟才需要高压锅，而密封高压锅把压强提到约两个标准大气压、沸点升到约 120 ℃（口径见「物态变化」条）；客机在一万米巡航，舱内必须增压到相当于两三千米高度的气压，否则人会在几分钟内失能。测量仪器有两类：水银气压计精度最高、气象台沿用已久，无液气压计靠抽成真空的金属盒随气压胀缩、便于携带，加上高度刻度就是高度计，登山表和飞机高度表都是它。最后一条常被问起：人体表面积约 1.6 平方米，大气压在上面留下的总压力约 1.6×10⁵ 牛、合十几吨重，人之所以没有被压扁，是因为体腔与体液内部的压强与外界随时平衡——大气压不是只从上面压下来，而是四面八方都在压，这与「液体压强」里同一深度各方压强相等的结论同源。
detailEn: Air has weight and flows, so gravity holds it in a shell around Earth where, like a liquid, it presses in every direction. This is atmospheric pressure, about 1.01×10⁵ Pa, or 101.3 kilopascals, at sea level. Torricelli measured it first: in 1644 he filled a roughly one-metre tube closed at one end with mercury, inverted it into a dish, and the column fell to a level about 760 mm above the dish, leaving near-vacuum above it — the Torricellian vacuum. His p=ρgh gives 13600×9.8×0.760, precisely 1.01×10⁵ Pa. The experiment carries its own control: if the atmosphere is holding the mercury up, water would need a tube over ten metres long (101325/(1000×9.8) is about 10.3 m), and that number fixes the limit of every suction pump. In 1654 von Guericke staged the Magdeburg hemispheres publicly, evacuating two copper shells that needed eight pairs of horses — sixteen in all — to part; a hemisphere of 0.25 m radius presents some 0.2 m², so the air pressed with roughly 2×10⁴ N, a two-tonne pull. Suction cups, drinking straws and pumps all run on pressure differences, though one phrase should be corrected: sipping is not pulling the drink up but lowering the pressure in your mouth so the atmosphere pushes the liquid up, and a piston pump likewise makes a low-pressure region for the water to rise into, yet one atmosphere can lift water only about 10.3 m. That is the ceiling on suction lift, which is why deep wells use centrifugal pumps with the impeller dropped below the waterline, submersible pumps, or staged lifting, while tall buildings do the opposite and feed from a roof tank or a booster set — a 30 m head supplies about 2.9×10⁵ Pa, matching domestic water pressure of 0.2 to 0.4 MPa. Pressure falls with altitude because the column overhead shortens; near the ground each 12 m of climb drops the mercury about a millimetre. Lhasa at 3650 m sees roughly 60 kilopascals, so water boils at 86 ℃ and rice undercooks, which is why a sealed pressure cooker raises the pressure to about two atmospheres and the boiling point to some 120 ℃, as the entry on changes of state records. Airliners cruising at ten kilometres must pressurise the cabin to the equivalent of two or three thousand metres, or crew and passengers are incapacitated within minutes. Two instruments serve: the mercury barometer, the most accurate and long used by weather services, and the aneroid barometer, where an evacuated metal box breathes with pressure, portable and — given an altitude scale — an altimeter, the same device in watches and aircraft. One last question: our roughly 1.6 m² of skin bears some 1.6×10⁵ N, a dozen tonnes of push, and we are not crushed because internal pressures balance it everywhere at once. The atmosphere presses from all sides, not merely downward, exactly as liquid pressure at a given depth acts equally in every direction.

oneLiner: 浸入液体的物体受到向上托力，大小等于它排开液体所受的重力。
oneLinerEn: A body in fluid is lifted by a force equal to the weight of fluid it displaces.
detail: 浸入液体或气体里的物体受到向上的托力，叫浮力，其大小由阿基米德原理给出：F浮=ρ液gV排，即浮力等于物体排开的那部分流体所受的重力，式中 ρ液 是流体密度、V排 是排开流体的体积。这一定律的出处是叙拉古国王希耶罗二世怀疑金匠在王冠里掺了银，阿基米德在浴室里注意到水被身体排开，想到用等重的纯金块与王冠各放入盛满水的容器比较溢出的水量——掺银的王冠体积更大、溢水更多，密度之说由此落地，后来他写成《论浮体》。实验上最常用的判据是称重法：先在空气中称出物重 G，再浸没在液体里称得示重 F示，则 F浮=G−F示。浮力的来源不是某种新力，而是「液体压强」的直接后果：下表面所处的深度更大、压强更大，上下表面的压力差合出一个向上的力，侧向的压力则逐对抵消。浮沉要看两个量的比较：浸没时若 F浮小于 G 就下沉，相等则悬浮在任何深度，大于则上浮，最后露出液面达到漂浮，此时 F浮=G 且 V排 只算浸入部分。所有能浮的器械都是在调这两个量之一。轮船把钢材做成空心，让几千吨钢板排出上万吨海水——排水量一万吨的轮船排开 10⁷ 千克水，浮力约 9.8×10⁷ 牛，恰与船重相抵；从海里驶入河里，水密度从约 1025 降到 1000 千克每立方米，排开体积必须增大，吃水随之加深约百分之二点五，所以船身上同时标有海水与淡水两条吃水线。潜水艇走的是另一条路：水舱灌海水就下潜、用高压气吹出水就上浮，它改变的是自身重力而浮力几乎不变。气球与飞艇靠空气浮力，1 立方米氢气受到约 12.6 牛浮力、氢气自身只重约 0.9 牛，净举力约 11.8 牛，热空气每秒只能挣出约 1.9 牛，所以热气球必须做到几万立方米。密度计漂浮时重力不变，浮力也就必须不变，液体越密它排开越少、露出越多，因此刻度上小下大、且因深度与密度成反比而不均匀。几个日常判据：死海盐度高达两成以上、密度约 1.2×10³ 千克每立方米，人能仰浮在水面；农业用适当浓度的盐水选种，饱满种粒密度大而下沉、虫蛀空粒上浮；冰山水下部分约占九成（917/1025≈89.5%），故“冰山一角”有真实的数字依据；汤圆与饺子煮熟浮起，是因为受热后内部气体膨胀、体积变大而重力几乎不变。两处易错必须点明：一是物体一旦完全浸没，浮力就与深度无关，“越深浮力越小”是错的，下沉时变的是压强而不是浮力；二是沉底的物体依然受浮力，除非它的下表面与容器底紧密贴合、液体进不去（打入河床的桥墩就是这种情形，这也是浮力公式的前提之一）。
detailEn: A body immersed in a liquid or a gas is pressed upward by buoyancy, whose size Archimedes' principle fixes: the buoyant force equals the weight of the fluid displaced, F = rho-fluid × g × V-displaced, where rho is the fluid's density and V the displaced volume. The story is Hiero II of Syracuse suspecting that a goldsmith had adulterated his crown, and Archimedes noticing in a bath how water gave way to his body: weighed against an equal lump of pure gold, the crown overflowed more water, meaning a larger volume and so a lower density — a test he later formalised in On Floating Bodies. The laboratory criterion is the weighing method: find the weight in air G, then the reading while immersed, and the buoyant force is their difference. Buoyancy is no new kind of force but the direct consequence of liquid pressure — the lower face sits deeper, feels more pressure, and the difference of the two faces sums to an upward push while sideways pushes cancel in pairs. Whether a body rises or sinks compares two quantities: submerged, it sinks if buoyancy falls short of weight, hangs suspended if they match, rises if buoyancy wins, and finally floats with buoyancy equal to weight and only the immersed volume counting as displaced. Every floating machine tunes one of them. Ships hollow out steel so thousands of tonnes of plate can displace tens of thousands of tonnes of water: a liner of 10 000 tonnes displacement pushes aside 10⁷ kg of seawater, giving 9.8×10⁷ N of lift to balance its weight, and steaming from sea into river, where density drops from about 1025 to 1000 kg per cubic metre, must displace more and so sits some 2.5 per cent deeper — hence separate salt and fresh water load lines on the hull. Submarines take the other route, flooding ballast to dive and blowing it out with high-pressure air to surface: they change their own weight while buoyancy barely moves. Balloons and airships ride air's buoyancy — a cubic metre of hydrogen is lifted with about 12.6 N and weighs only 0.9 N of itself, a net 11.8 N, whereas hot air earns barely 1.9 N, which is why hot-air envelopes must reach tens of thousands of cubic metres. A hydrometer floats with fixed weight and therefore fixed buoyancy, so denser liquids displace less and it stands higher: its scale reads small at the top, large at the bottom, and is uneven because depth varies inversely with density. Everyday tests: the Dead Sea, over one fifth salt and about 1.2×10³ kg per cubic metre, holds a person on its surface; farmers brine-sort seed so plump grains sink and worm-eaten ones float; nine tenths of an iceberg (917/1025 is 89.5 per cent) lies below the waterline, giving 'tip of the iceberg' an honest number; dumplings and glutinous balls rise when cooked because heating expands their volume while their weight hardly changes. Two slips must be named. Once a body is fully submerged buoyancy stops caring about depth — 'deeper means less lift' is wrong; what grows with depth is pressure. And a sunken body still feels buoyancy unless its underside is sealed against the container floor so no fluid gets in, the case of a bridge pile driven into riverbed mud, which is itself a hidden premise of the formula.

oneLiner: 流体流速大的地方压强小，产生升力与吸附现象。
oneLinerEn: Faster flow means lower pressure, producing lift and suction.
detail: 在同一个稳定流动里，流速大的地方压强小，这就是流体压强与流速的关系，1738 年丹尼尔·伯努利在《流体学》中给出这一结论，今天常见的公式形式由欧拉在十八世纪中叶整理出来：沿同一条流线，p+½ρv²+ρgh 保持不变，三项分别是压强能、动能与势能的份额，所以它的实质是能量守恒在流体里的写法（口径见「机械能守恒」条）。使用前提要写足：同一流体、稳定流动、不可压缩、比较的两点在同一条流线上，四个条件少一个就不能直接下结论。机翼升力是最有名的例子：教材按“上表面凸、气流路程长而流速大、压强小”讲它，严格说法还要补一句——升力同时来自机翼把气流往下偏折，被偏折的空气给机翼向上的反作用（见「牛顿第三定律」条），压差与偏转本是同一件事的两面，而“上下两股空气必须同时到达后缘”的等时假设并不成立。攻角是机翼与来流的夹角，增大攻角能增大升力，超过约十几度后气流在上表面分离、升力骤降，就是失速。算一笔账：6×10⁴ 千克的客机需要约 5.9×10⁵ 牛升力，摊在 125 平方米的机翼上只需约 4.7×10³ 帕的压强差，不到大气压的百分之五；按 Δp=½ρ(v₂²−v₁²) 反推，若下表面气流约 70 米每秒，上表面约 113 米每秒就够了。两船并行之所以相吸，是中间水道变窄、流速增大、压强降低（判据在「流量与连续性」条），十九世纪初以来多起轮船与军舰贴近相撞都被这样解释，因此各国都规定了追越时的横距；火车站与地铁站的安全线同理，列车以 80 千米每小时（约 22 米每秒）掠过时，人身迎风面与背风面的压差可达约 290 帕，作用在 1 平方米上就是约 290 牛的推力，足以把人推向轨道。足球的香蕉球与乒乓球的上旋下旋出自同一机理：旋转的球带动边界层空气，两侧流速不等便有了侧向压强差，这叫马格努斯效应。喷雾器、化油器与老式香水瓶靠的是“低压抽液”：高速气流经过细管口使管口压强低于大气压，液体被压上来并被吹散成雾。飞机的空速管（皮托管）把迎面气流的总压与侧孔的静压相减，用 v=√(2Δp/ρ) 反算速度，压差 3000 帕约对应 71 米每秒即 255 千米每小时，赛车与风力发电测试也用同一把尺。大风掀掉屋顶也是这条规律：屋面上方风速大而屋内气压照常，30 米每秒的风在 100 平方米屋面上能交出约 5.5 吨的举力，所以抗风设计要算屋面的向上净压。两处易错要挑明：一、不能拿两处的“流速”和「压强」随意配对比较，必须在同一流线上，否则会出现“吹两张纸反而分开”这类误判；二、气体压强变化大时密度也变，伯努利式要修正，超音速流动另有规矩。
detailEn: Within one steady flow, faster fluid presses less: this is the relation between fluid speed and pressure, given by Daniel Bernoulli in his Hydrodynamica of 1738 and written into today's form by Euler in the mid eighteenth century — along a single streamline, p plus a half rho v-squared plus rho gh stays constant, the three terms being shares of pressure energy, kinetic energy and potential energy, so the statement is really energy conservation told for fluids, the same ledger as the entry on conservation of mechanical energy. Its conditions must be stated in full: one and the same fluid, steady flow, essentially incompressible, and both comparison points lying on the same streamline; drop any of them and the conclusion no longer follows. Lift on a wing is the famous case. Textbooks say the curved upper surface makes air travel farther and faster, so pressure falls; the rigorous version adds that a wing also deflects the oncoming air downwards and the deflected air pushes the wing up (see the entry on Newton's third law), pressure difference and deflection being two faces of one fact, while the 'equal transit time' claim — that two parcels parted at the leading edge must reunite at the trailing edge — is simply false. Angle of attack, the tilt between wing and oncoming flow, raises lift until some ten-odd degrees, when the flow separates from the upper surface and lift collapses: that is a stall. Do the arithmetic. A 6×10⁴ kg airliner needs about 5.9×10⁵ N, and spread over 125 m² of wing this is a pressure gap of only 4.7×10³ Pa, under five per cent of an atmosphere; inverting delta-p equals a half rho times the difference of squares gives about 113 m/s over the top where the underside sees 70 m/s. Two ships running parallel are drawn together because the narrowed channel speeds the water and lowers its pressure — the criterion belongs to the entry on flow rate and continuity — and close-quarter collisions between ships have been read this way for two centuries, which is why passing distances are legislated. Platform safety lines follow the same rule: a train arriving at 80 km/h, some 22 m/s, can leave a pressure gap near 290 Pa across a person, roughly 290 N pushing on one square metre of chest, quite enough to shove someone onto the track. The bending free kick and the spinning ping-pong ball come from the same mechanism, the Magnus effect: a spinning ball drags boundary-layer air so the two sides differ in speed and therefore in pressure. Atomisers, carburettors and old perfume bulbs all draw liquid up into a fast stream, where the nozzle pressure falls below atmosphere and the liquid is lifted and shredded into spray. An aircraft's pitot tube subtracts static pressure from the stagnation pressure it gathers head-on and recovers speed as v equals the square root of two delta-p over rho: 3000 Pa of difference corresponds to about 71 m/s, near 255 km/h, and the same probe serves racing cars and wind-turbine tests. Roofs torn off in storms are Bernoulli's too: fast wind above an intact pressure indoors, and 30 m/s over 100 m² yields a lifting force around five tonnes, so wind-resistant design counts that upward net load. Two errors deserve naming. You may not pair 'speed here' with 'pressure there' at will — the comparison must run along one streamline, otherwise demonstrations such as blowing between two sheets get misread. And when a gas changes pressure greatly its density changes as well, so Bernoulli's equation needs correction and supersonic flow plays by different rules.

oneLiner: 液体表面像一层绷紧的薄膜，使液滴收成球形、让轻小物体浮于水面。
oneLinerEn: A liquid's surface acts like a stretched skin, beading drops and holding light objects afloat.
detail: 液体表面层像一张被绷紧的薄膜，这个说法背后是很具体的分子账：表面层的分子与内部分子相比，上方缺少同伴，受到内部分子的引力没有被抵消，于是整层被往里拉，表面自发收缩，宏观上就表现为沿表面切向作用的张力。描述它的物理量是张力系数 σ，定义为一段边界单位长度受到的拉力，单位牛每米，也可看成每增加一平方米表面所需的能量；水在 20 ℃ 时约 0.073 牛每米，肥皂水降到约 0.025，酒精约 0.022，水银高达约 0.46，所以水银滴圆得发硬。正因为表面要收缩，同体积下表面积最小的形状就是球形，露珠、熔化的金属滴与蜡滴才都收成球。弯曲表面还会造成压强差，球面的附加压强为 Δp=2σ/R，半径 1 毫米的水泡内外只差约 146 帕，与大气压相比是千分之一，可一旦半径缩到微米量级，这个压差就爬到与大气压可比的地步——表面效应在小尺度上称王，这也是两个相同的小气泡相连后小者会被大者吸空的原因。表面张力能托住比水重的东西：缝衣针或单面刀片小心地横放在水面上可以浮着，它排开的体积微小到浮力几乎为零，靠的全是这张膜；一只约 20 毫克的水黾六条腿压在面上，与水面接触的总长约 2 厘米，σL 最多能交出约 1.5×10⁻³ 牛的向上托力，是它体重的七倍上下。这里必须分清浮力与表面张力两种机制，「浮力与阿基米德原理」条管的是排开液体的重力。与表面紧密相关的一对概念是浸润与不浸润：液体与固体接触的附着层里，若固体分子对液体分子的引力强过液体内聚力，附着层就扩张、液面贴壁铺开，称浸润，水对洁净玻璃、酒精对大多数表面都属此类，接触角小于 90°；反之附着层收缩、液体缩成团，称不浸润，水银在玻璃上、水在蜡与荷叶上都是典型，接触角大于 90°。荷叶把不浸润推到极致：叶面微米级的乳突与蜡质共同把接触角抬到 150° 以上，滚落的水珠顺带粘走灰尘，这就是自洁的荷叶效应，它与「毛细现象」条同源，都发生在附着层上。工程与家务里的应用也多依此：焊接时撒的助焊剂既除氧化膜又降低熔融锡的表面张力，让锡铺开润湿铜面；肥皂与洗涤剂一方面把水的张力压下一大截、使水能钻进织物缝隙，另一方面靠分子一端亲水一端亲油把油污乳化成微小液滴（乳化本身在「万物化学」科目里另有说法）；陶瓷注浆、油漆涂装、 打印纸张吸墨、土壤持水都涉及同一枚硬币的两面。三条易错：一、表面张力的方向沿液面切向、不是垂直压向液面；二、它是分子引力的宏观表现，而不是分子斥力；三、温度升高时张力系数明显下降，热水比冷水更容易润湿与铺开。
detailEn: A liquid's surface behaves like a stretched skin, and the molecular bookkeeping behind that image is concrete: a molecule in the surface layer lacks neighbours above, so the pull of the liquid below it is not cancelled and the whole layer is dragged inward, the surface contracting of its own accord and showing up macroscopically as a force tangent to the surface. The quantity describing it is the tension coefficient, defined as the pull per unit length of boundary in newtons per metre, or equivalently the energy needed to create a square metre of fresh surface: water at 20 ℃ sits near 0.073 N/m, soapy water falls to about 0.025, alcohol to 0.022, mercury climbs to roughly 0.46, which is why mercury beads look rigidly round. Because the surface is trying to shrink, the shape with least area for a given volume wins, and dewdrops, molten metal droplets and wax drops all pull themselves spherical. A curved surface also costs pressure: for a spherical interface the extra pressure is two sigma over R. A one-millimetre bubble differs from its surroundings by only about 146 Pa, a thousandth of an atmosphere, yet shrink the radius to micrometres and that gap grows to atmospheric scale — surface effects rule the small world, which is why two connected small bubbles empty the smaller into the larger. Surface tension can hold up things denser than water: a sewing needle or a single-edge blade laid carefully on the surface will stay afloat though the buoyant force from displaced liquid is negligible, carried entirely by the film; a water strider of some 20 milligrams presses six legs onto the surface over a total contact length near two centimetres, so sigma times length supplies up to about 1.5×10⁻³ N, some seven times its weight. Buoyancy and film tension must be kept apart here — the entry on buoyancy counts the weight of displaced fluid, this one counts a skin. A closely related pair of ideas is wetting and non-wetting. In the adhesion layer touching a solid, if the solid's pull on liquid molecules beats the liquid's cohesion, that layer spreads and the liquid climbs and flattens — we call it wetting, as water does on clean glass or alcohol on nearly anything, contact angle below 90 degrees; when the adhesion layer contracts instead, the liquid balls up — non-wetting, as mercury on glass or water on wax — with contact angle above 90 degrees. The lotus pushes non-wetting to its limit: microscopic bumps plus a wax coating lift the contact angle past 150 degrees, so rolling beads gather dust and clean the leaf, the self-cleaning lotus effect, whose mechanism is shared with the entry on capillary action since both live in the adhesion layer. Applications turn on the same coin's two faces: flux in soldering both strips the oxide film and lowers the surface tension of molten tin so it wets copper; soap and detergents cut water's tension sharply so it penetrates cloth, while their molecules — water-loving at one end, oil-loving at the other — emulsify grease into tiny droplets, a chemist's topic in its own right; slip casting of ceramics, painting, ink-jet paper and soil moisture all obey the same rules. Three slips are worth naming. Surface tension acts tangentially along the surface, never pressing perpendicular into it. It is the macroscopic face of molecular attraction, not of repulsion. And the coefficient falls visibly as temperature rises, which is why hot water wets and spreads better than cold.

oneLiner: 细管中的液面会自动升高或下降，管越细现象越明显。
oneLinerEn: Liquid climbs or falls in narrow tubes, and the thinner the tube the stronger the effect.
detail: 把细管插进能浸润它的液体里，液面会自己升到高于容器液面，管子越细升得越高；换成不浸润的液体（如水银在玻璃管里），液面反而被压低——这就是毛细现象，常见于半径零点几毫米以下的细管、缝隙与多孔材料。它的成因是「表面张力」与浸润两件事的合力：浸润的液体在附着层被管壁拉向上方，弯月面因此凹下去，一张绷紧的膜在弯曲面上交出附加压强，把液体往上提，直到被提起的液柱重力把压强差抵消为止。把这个平衡写成公式就是 h=2σcosθ/(ρgr)，式中 σ 为张力系数、θ 为接触角、r 为管半径。数值最能说明它有多依赖尺度：水在半径 0.1 毫米的玻璃管里约升 15 厘米，10 微米的管里约 1.5 米，1 微米的缝里理论上可达 15 米；同样道理，砖块、混凝土、石膏板能把地下水沿孔隙举到墙上，形成“返潮”与盐霜，老建筑的地圈梁与防潮层就是在切断这条通路。生活中的名单还很长：纸巾与吸墨纸吸墨、毛笔与钢笔尖储墨、油灯与酒精灯把燃料从储液池沿棉灯芯举到灯头燃烧、蜡烛芯同理、方糖与面包沿孔隙吸咖啡、土壤里的水分被举到地表蒸发。最后一条牵出一个重要的农业经验：锄松表层土壤是为了切断土壤里的毛细管，让下层水分不再被举到表面白白蒸发，北方农谚所谓“锄头三寸泽”。有一处最常被混谈的账要算清：高大的树木并不是靠毛细现象喝水的。木质部导管的半径在微米量级，按上式毛细至多把水举几米到十几米，而几十米高的红杉要把水送到树冠，主要动力来自叶片气孔蒸腾拉出的水柱张力——水分子之间的内聚力让这条细水柱能够承受拉力而不被拉断，毛细只在幼苗、表层土壤与叶片末端起辅助作用。蒸腾作用在「万物生物」与「万物地理」两科里各有专条，此处只强调力学分工。三条易错：一、毛细上升的高度与管半径成反比，与管长无关，管子太短时液体升到管口就停住而不会喷出来；二、液体必须浸润管壁才会上升，不浸润时方向相反，这也是水银气压计里读数要修正弯月面的原因；三、毛细管必须上端开口与大气相通，封闭的管里被压出的气体很快就会把上升顶回去。
detailEn: Plunge a slender tube into a liquid it can wet and the liquid climbs above the surrounding level, higher the narrower the bore; swap in a liquid the tube will not wet, mercury in glass for instance, and the level is depressed instead. This is capillary action, usual in tubes, slits and porous materials with radii below a fraction of a millimetre. Its cause is the joint venture of surface tension and wetting described in those entries: in the adhesion layer the wetted liquid is tugged upward by the wall, the meniscus turns concave, and a stretched curved skin supplies an extra pressure that lifts the column until the weight of the raised liquid cancels it. Written as an equation the balance reads h equals two sigma cosine theta over rho g r, sigma being the tension coefficient, theta the contact angle and r the tube radius. Numbers show how fiercely the effect depends on scale: water climbs some 15 centimetres in a glass tube of 0.1 millimetre radius, about 1.5 metres at 10 micrometres and in principle 15 metres in a one-micrometre slit. For the same reason bricks, concrete and plaster wick groundwater up into walls, producing damp and salt blooms, which is why older buildings carry a damp-proof course — a deliberate cut across that pathway. The household list runs long: blotting paper and tissues drawing ink, brush and fountain-pen tips holding their supply, oil lamps and spirit lamps lifting fuel along a cotton wick to the burner, candle wicks doing the same, a sugar cube or bread soaking up coffee through its pores, soil raising water to the surface where it evaporates. That last item carries an old farming lesson: hoeing breaks the surface into a loose layer, severing the capillary channels so that subsoil moisture is no longer wicked up and lost — the reason behind the proverb that a hoe holds three inches of rain. One widely confused account must be settled: tall trees do not drink by capillarity. Xylem conduits have radii in the micrometre range, so capillary lift tops out at a few to a dozen metres, whereas a redwood scores of metres high moves water to its crown mainly by the tension drawn by transpiration from leaf pores — cohesion between water molecules lets a thread of sap bear a pull without snapping — capillarity assisting only in seedlings, topsoil and the leaf end. Transpiration has its own entries in the biology and geography subjects; here only the mechanical division of labour matters. Three slips are worth naming. Capillary height varies inversely with radius and not with tube length, so a short tube simply fills to its mouth and stops rather than jetting. The liquid must wet the wall to rise; otherwise the shift is downward, which is why mercury barometer readings are corrected for their meniscus. And the tube must stay open to the atmosphere, since in a closed one the compressed trapped air soon pushes the rise back down.

oneLiner: 流体内部阻碍各层相对滑动的「内摩擦」，蜂蜜比水黏得多。
oneLinerEn: Internal friction resisting layers sliding past one another; honey is far more viscous than water.
detail: 流体的黏性是流体内部阻碍各层相对滑动的“内摩擦”。它与固体摩擦的口径不同：固体的滑动摩擦发生在接触面、大小近似与正压力成正比；黏性阻力发生在流体内部相邻两快慢层之间，与两层的接触面积和速度梯度成正比，写成 F=ηS·Δv/Δx，静止的流体里它完全不露面。描述黏性大小的量是黏度 η，单位帕·秒：水在 20 ℃ 约 1.0×10⁻³，血液约 3 到 4×10⁻³，比水黏三成到四成，蜂蜜约 10、番茄酱更达上百，比水大一万到几万倍，空气约 1.8×10⁻⁵，是水的五十分之一——“黏”与“稠”的日常感觉与数量级关系相当不可靠，酒精与水的黏度同量级却显得“稀”，甘油黏而密度并不特别高。温度效应在两类流体里方向相反，这一点最容易记错：液体升温黏度下降，蜂蜜泡进热水就流动起来，发动机冬天要用低黏度的 5W 机油才转得动；气体升温黏度上升，因为分子热运动更剧烈、层与层之间交换动量更快（与「分子动理论」条的口径一致）。黏性最直观的后果是层流与湍流之分：流线平滑、分层滑行的叫层流，充满旋涡、彼此掺混的叫湍流，判据是无量纲的雷诺数 Re=ρvL/η，圆管里大约 2000 以下层流、4000 以上湍流。算几个例子就明白为什么水管里几乎总是湍流：内径 2 厘米、每秒 1 米的水流 Re 约 2×10⁴，早就过了临界，所以水龙头开到后面水柱会“抖”；而人体主动脉里血流 Re 只有约 500，属层流，瓣膜狭窄处 Re 上千、开始湍，医生用听诊器听到的杂音正是这种湍流的证据；毛细血管中速度只有约 0.5 毫米每秒、直径几微米，Re 低至千分之一量级，黏性完全压过惯性，血流在此最慢也最平稳，气体交换因此得以完成。两条定量规律最常用。一是斯托克斯定律：小球在黏滞流体中低速运动时阻力 F=6πηrv，与「密立根油滴实验」条同源——半径 0.5 微米的油滴在空气里的收尾速度只有约 30 微米每秒，慢到这个地步才让密立根能把单颗油滴反复悬停、倒退着测量它的电荷；而收尾速度本身仍是力学里“阻力增大到与重力相等即匀速”那件事，见「匀速直线运动」条。二是泊肃叶定律：细管中层流的流量 Q=πr⁴Δp/(8ηL)，与管径的四次方成反比，血管半径收缩一半血流量只剩十六分之一，这就是血压调节几乎全靠改变血管口径的道理，也解释了为什么狭窄的血管需要显著更高的压强才能维持供血。工程与自然的例子遍布：机油牌号、润滑与轴承发热、泥浆与混凝土的泵送、船体的摩擦阻力、蜂蜜与熔岩的缓慢流动，而岩浆是极说明问题的一例——硅含量高、黏度大的岩浆里气体跑不出来，压力攒够就爆炸式喷发；玄武岩岩浆黏度低，气体从容逸出，就安静地溢成熔岩流。两条易错要挑明：一、黏度大不代表密度大，两件事互不蕴含；二、静止流体里不表现为黏性力，只有层间发生相对滑动时才有，所以“黏”的是速度差而不是运动本身。
detailEn: Viscosity is internal friction: a fluid's own reluctance to let one layer slide past another. Its accounting differs from that of solid friction, which lives at a contact surface and scales with the normal load, whereas viscous drag arises between neighbouring fast and slow layers inside the fluid, proportional to their contact area and to the velocity gradient, written F equals eta S times delta-v over delta-x, and it stays entirely invisible in a fluid at rest. The measure is the viscosity eta in pascal seconds: water at 20 ℃ about 1.0×10⁻³, blood three to four times that, honey near 10 and tomato sauce into the hundreds — ten thousand to a hundred thousand times water — while air sits at 1.8×10⁻⁵, a fiftieth of water. Everyday words such as 'thick' are unreliable across scales: alcohol feels thin yet is close to water in viscosity, and glycerine is stiff without being unusually dense. Temperature pulls the two classes in opposite directions, the point most often misremembered: liquids thin out when heated — honey runs once warmed in hot water, and engines need low-viscosity 5W oil to turn over in winter — while gases thicken, because faster molecular motion shuttles momentum between layers more briskly, in the same spirit as the entry on kinetic molecular theory. Viscosity's most visible consequence is the split between laminar and turbulent flow: smooth sliding layers against churning, mixing eddies. The criterion is the dimensionless Reynolds number, Re equals rho v L over eta; in pipes flow stays laminar below roughly 2000 and turns turbulent above 4000. A few sums explain why taps are almost always turbulent: water moving a metre per second through a 2-centimetre bore gives Re near 20 000, well past the limit, which is why the jet starts to shake further downstream. Blood in the aorta, by contrast, sits near Re 500 and streams in orderly layers, while a narrowed valve pushes Re past a thousand and turbulence begins — the murmur a physician hears is exactly that turbulence. In capillaries, where speed is about half a millimetre per second across a few micrometres, Re drops to a thousandth, viscosity utterly dominates inertia, and the resulting slowness is what lets gas exchange finish in peace. Two quantitative laws earn their keep. Stokes' law gives the drag on a small sphere creeping through a viscous fluid, F equals six pi eta r v — the same physics as the entry on Millikan's oil-drop experiment: an oil drop half a micrometre in radius falls through air at only some 30 micrometres per second, and it is precisely this slowness that let Millikan hover a single drop and walk it backwards to measure its charge. That steady terminal speed is still the mechanics story of drag growing until it matches weight, as the entry on uniform motion notes. Poiseuille's law says that laminated flow through a thin tube carries Q equals pi r to the fourth delta-p over 8 eta L, so radius matters to the fourth power: halve a vessel and the flow drops to a sixteenth, which is why blood-pressure control works almost entirely by changing vessel calibre, and why a narrowed artery needs a much higher pressure to sustain supply. Examples litter engineering and nature: oil grades, bearing warmth, pumping mud and concrete, a hull's skin friction, honey and lava creeping downhill. Magma makes the case crisply — silica-rich, stiff magma traps its gases until pressure builds and the eruption goes explosive, while runny basalt lets gas escape and simply overflows into lava flows. Two slips to name: high viscosity does not imply high density, the two being unrelated; and viscous force exists only when layers actually slide on each other, so what a fluid resists is the velocity difference, not motion itself.

oneLiner: 稳定流动中，同一流体通过任一截面的流量相等，管细处流速必大。
oneLinerEn: In steady flow the same fluid carries equal volume rate through every cross-section, so narrower parts run faster.
detail: 流量指单位时间流过某一截面的流体体积，记 Q=Sv，单位是立方米每秒，家用软管放水约 5 升每秒即 5×10⁻³ 立方米每秒。连续性方程说的是一条守恒：在同一段没有分支、没有源也没有汇的流管里，稳定流动时流过每个截面的流量必须相等，否则流体要么在中间堆积要么被拉断，于是 S₁v₁=S₂v₂，式中 S 为截面积、v 为该截面上的平均流速，结论就是截面积与流速成反比。它的前提同样要写清楚：流体不可压缩（或密度近似不变）、流动稳定、比较的是同一股流体。数值最有说服力：5 升每秒的水在直径 10 厘米的管里平均只有 0.64 米每秒，被压进 2.5 厘米的细管就飙到 10.2 米每秒——速度涨了十六倍，而黏性造成的压强损失大致随速度平方上升，所以给水管不能一味缩径，泵要为此多付功（代价见「流体的黏性」条）。日常与工程现象一串可举：用手指捏窄水管口，水柱变细而出口速度更大、射程更远，园林喷嘴与洗车水枪就是这个把手，要注意的是流量并没有变大，变的只是速度与形态；河流在狭窄处水急、在开阔处水缓，航行的船只在浅窄航道里会被加速并难以操纵；地铁列车进站的瞬间像一支巨型针筒，把隧道里的空气沿活塞效应推向站台，站台门与通风口的布置正是按这条规律设计的；火箭与喷气发动机的喷管先收缩后扩张，称为拉瓦尔喷管。最后一条需要一个补充：气体速度接近或超过声速时密度不能再当作常数，守恒式要写成 ρ₁S₁v₁=ρ₂S₂v₂，于是在超音速段“截面越大速度反而越快”，与低速水的直觉正好相反，这正是喷管必须先收后放的原因。生物体也按同一式子分配流速，但要看清一个陷阱：血管与气管一级级分支，单根越来越细，可是分支数量增加得更快，总截面积反而逐级增大，因此速度逐级下降——全身最慢的血流出现在总截面最大的毛细血管网，肺里气流在肺泡附近近乎停下，两者都为了让交换有时间发生，这与「流体的黏性」条里毛细血管雷诺数极低的说法互相印证。三条易错要点明：一、连续性讲的是同一股流体在两个截面之间的比较，不能拿来比两根不同的管或两台不同的泵；二、截面积小处速度大并不表示流量大，各截面流量处处相同；三、它只在不可压缩与稳定流动的前提下精确成立，有水锤、进气或可燃混合气脉动的场合要另行处理。
detailEn: Flow rate is the volume of fluid crossing a given section per second, Q equals S v, in cubic metres per second; a garden hose letting out five litres a second is running at 5×10⁻³ cubic metres per second. The continuity equation states one conservation claim: inside a stretch of flow that branches nowhere and has neither source nor sink, steady motion must carry the same flow rate through every section, otherwise fluid would pile up or snap apart, hence S1 v1 equals S2 v2, where S is cross-sectional area and v the mean speed over it, and the consequence is that area and speed trade inversely. Its premises deserve writing down as well: the fluid is incompressible or nearly so, the flow is steady, and the comparison concerns one and the same stream. Numbers carry the argument. Five litres a second moves at an average 0.64 metres per second in a 10-centimetre pipe but shoots to 10.2 metres per second squeezed into a 25-millimetre bore — sixteen times faster, while viscous loss of pressure rises roughly with the square of speed, so supply pipes cannot simply be narrowed and the pump must pay extra work for it, the cost recorded in the entry on viscosity. A string of familiar cases follows. Pinching a hose's mouth makes the jet thinner and faster and it reaches farther, the trick behind lawn nozzles and car-wash lances, though the flow rate has not grown — only the speed and the shape of the stream. Rivers quicken in narrows and slacken in open reaches, which is why ships feel pulled and hard to steer in a shallow constricted channel. A metro train entering a station acts as a giant syringe, ramming tunnel air ahead of it onto the platform by piston effect, and platform doors and ventilation grilles are laid out by exactly this rule. Rocket and jet nozzles contract then expand, the de Laval shape. That last case needs a supplement: once gas speed approaches or exceeds sound, density can no longer be treated as constant, the conservation law becomes rho1 S1 v1 equals rho2 S2 v2, and in the supersonic leg a wider section means a faster flow — the opposite of the low-speed water intuition, which is precisely why the nozzle must first pinch and then flare. Living bodies apportion speed by the same equation, but here a trap must be cleared. Blood vessels and airways branch level after level, each tube getting thinner, yet the number of branches grows faster still, so total cross-sectional area climbs stage by stage and speed falls stage by stage: the slowest blood in the body is in the capillary bed, which has by far the greatest total area, and airflow in the lung all but stalls near the alveoli, both because exchange needs time. That agrees with the capillary Reynolds numbers so tiny that viscosity rules, as the entry on viscosity notes. Three slips deserve naming. Continuity compares two sections of one and the same stream, not two different pipes or two different pumps. A smaller area with a higher speed does not mean a bigger flow rate, since the rate is the same everywhere along the stream. And it holds exactly only for incompressible, steady motion; water hammer, ingested air or pulsing fuel mixture each require separate treatment.
